It was also stated that she was pushed in a well and was subsequently, taken out of the well with the help of villagers.

In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim reiterated the story and stated that the applicant had come alongwith her friend and both of them committed wrong on her and thereafter, pushed her in a well.
She also stated that another witness Kuntal had heard the voice of the victim and came and thereafter, with the help of villagers, she was taken outside the well.
The statement of the witness Kuntal is on record wherein she stated that she had heard the voice from the well and then she called the Ex-Pradhan and other villagers who pulled out the victim.
The medical on record done on 24.02.2024 does not indicate any injury whatsoever either on the external or in the internal parts of the victim.

4. In the light of the said allegation, learned counsel for the applicant argues that in the statement made before the medical authorities, allegations were levelled against two persons for committing wrong on her; no allegations of pushing her in a well were levelled.
5. Learned AGA, based upon the case diary, states that none of the witnesses who had allegedly taken out the victim from the well is on record except the statement of Kuntal.

6. Considering the materials on record, prima-facie, the allegations of the commission of the offence under Section 376 IPC are not corroborated by the medical on record; there are no witnesses to sustain the charge under Section 307 IPC.
As such, considering that evidence for both the charges is prima-facie not supporting the prosecution story

coupled with the fact that the tentative age of the victim is around 17 years as per the radiological examination, the applicant who is in custody since 25.02.2024 and has no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Vinod Kumar Prajapati be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
